clue.text: One captured by the enemy about to invite everyone in for a beer

indicators.note: 'about' as in turned about, so the abbreviation is read back to front
to invite someone in is to take them inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: a prisoner of war, abbreviated POW
everyone is all

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war whose captors are about to share a round of beer with everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'One captured by the enemy' describes a single abbreviation, the usual shorthand for a prisoner of war, rather than asking you to pick out 'one' as I or A.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallop is informal British slang for beer, especially strong cheap ale.

clue.text: Ultimately, Gabriel with Collins, for the listener a load of rubbish

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the name is kept
something meant for a listener is heard rather than read, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: the last letter of Gabriel
with means together with, and
Phil Collins, the Genesis drummer and singer

explanation.surface: A sneer at the music of Genesis: Peter Gabriel and Phil Collins together sound like rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Gabriel and Phil Collins were both singers in the band Genesis, so the surface reads as music criticism. Collins supplies his first name, Phil, which is heard as FILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A landfill is a site where household waste is buried, so it holds a huge heap of refuse.

clue.text: Wagner opera: nul points in Paris, almost the same in New York

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: French for nothing
American slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A review of a Wagner opera that scored zero with critics in both Paris and New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nul points' is the Eurovision score for a total flop, French for no points. French nothing is RIEN; New York nothing is ZIP, cut short to ZI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rienzi is an early grand opera by Richard Wagner, first staged in Dresden in 1842.

clue.text: 1978 film generates clue for g, say

blocks.note: the letter g sits in the middle of 'night', so 'midnight' could clue it
to express is to put out or produce

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a 1978 film and a crossword clue for the letter g.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as a sentence, 'midnight expresses g', is the joke: in crossword language mid-night is the middle letter of night. 'Say' marks this as one example of such a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Midnight Express is the Alan Parker prison drama of 1978, set in a Turkish jail.

clue.text: Piccolo is one overwhelmed by far too much wine, commonly

indicators.note: in a down entry, being overwhelmed means sitting beneath, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: over the top
one is a
informal word for wine

explanation.surface: A piccolo player swamped by an excess of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT, over the top, is British informal shorthand for excessive. 'Commonly' marks vino as a colloquial word for wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottavino is the Italian name for the piccolo, the small flute sounding an octave higher.

clue.text: Debt is problematic, finding a place to live

indicators.note: something problematic is in a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Money troubles push someone to find somewhere cheap to live.
explanation.walkthrough: A bedsit, a single rented room used for living and sleeping, is the classic British home for someone short of cash, so the answer suits the story.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedsit is a one-room rented lodging, a modest sort of home or dwelling.

clue.text: Students' Union: first I must leave for it to become more sovereign

indicators.note: whatever must leave is taken out of the word it was in

blocks.note: the initial letters of Students' Union
premier means first or foremost
the letter that is removed

explanation.surface: A students' union motion about ranking first, phrased like a rule of procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' looks like an instruction to take an initial letter, but it is the word PREMIER, from which the I is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in authority, and its comparative form expresses holding greater sovereign power.

clue.text: Italian musician at last eating a filling local sandwich (or two?)

indicators.note: 'at last' points to the final position, so only the closing letter of the next word is used
a filling is what goes in the middle of something, so these letters are placed inside the next piece

blocks.note: the Italian toasted sandwich; strictly the plural of panino, hence 'or two?'
the final letter of eating
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian musician finally having lunch, eating a filled sandwich from his home country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' ties the sandwich to the Italian of the definition. In Italian panini is the plural of panino, so strictly the word names two sandwiches, hence the '(or two?)'.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was the celebrated Italian violin virtuoso and composer of the early nineteenth century.

clue.text: Daily Star

blocks.note: first meaning: a newspaper published every day, here a British tabloid
second meaning: the star at the centre of our solar system

explanation.walkthrough: The italics make it look like the name of the British tabloid the Daily Star; split in two, each word defines the answer, itself the title of a rival tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a British daily newspaper, and the sun is the nearest star to Earth.

clue.text: Palestinians backed by Oxbridge academic make very slow progress

indicators.note: being backed by something means having it behind you, so the second piece comes after the first

blocks.note: the Palestine Liberation Organization
a don is a university teacher at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A Palestinian cause supported by a university lecturer, but getting nowhere fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' might suggest a reversal, but here it means supported from behind, so the academic simply follows. Oxbridge is the joint name for Oxford and Cambridge universities.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod on is to keep going with heavy, laborious steps, continuing at a slow, dogged pace.

clue.text: French tennis icon heading for Channel island in lifeboat?

blocks.note: Yannick Noah, winner of the 1983 French Open
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A French tennis star sailing off to a small island in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands lie off the coast of Normandy and include Jersey, Guernsey and Sark. The question mark admits the ark is a lifeboat only in a playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical ark carried Noah, his family and the animals safely through the Flood, saving their lives.

clue.text: Parcel company, mostly growing in reputation, causes a revolution

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: United Parcel Service, the delivery firm
a rising star is growing in reputation

explanation.surface: A delivery firm on the up, shaking up its whole industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Causes a revolution' sounds like business jargon for disruption, but 'a revolution' alone is the definition, joined by 'causes'.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a popular rebellion against those in power, which is what a revolution is.

clue.text: This bendy motorway's narrow passages

indicators.note: something bendy can be twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway, written with I for 1

explanation.surface: A complaint about a winding motorway with narrow lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; crosswords write it MI, treating the digit 1 as the letter I. The 's means 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Isthmi is a plural of isthmus, a narrow strip of land joining two larger landmasses.

clue.text: Takeaway at lunchtime?

blocks.note: surface reading: buying a hot meal to carry out in the middle of the day
setter's reading: a theft, a taking away, committed in broad daylight, also slang for an outrageous price

explanation.walkthrough: A takeaway is the British term for food bought to eat elsewhere; read literally, taking something away is stealing, and lunchtime is when the sun is high.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means blatant overcharging, a rip-off, and literally describes theft committed openly while it is light outside.

clue.text: Boy adopted by a rising celebrity in full agreement

indicators.note: someone adopted is taken into a family, so one piece is brought inside another
in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

blocks.note: a boy is a son
taken as written
a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A boy adopted by an up-and-coming star, with everyone agreeing it is a good thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A rising celebrity' sounds like one up-and-coming star, but 'a' stays as itself and only the celebrity word climbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To act as one man is an idiom for a group behaving with complete unanimity.

clue.text: Former democrat, American, seen in sports car, something difficult to obtain

indicators.note: to be seen in a vehicle is to be inside it, so these letters go within the next ones

blocks.note: old means former
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
abbreviation for United States
gran turismo, a grand touring car

explanation.surface: A former American politician spotted in a flashy sports car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former democrat' reads as one person, an ex-Democrat, but it splits into two pieces, the adjective and the party initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is like gold dust is a British idiom for it being scarce and highly sought after.

clue.text: Awesome skyward throw that's perplexing

indicators.note: in a down entry, going skyward means travelling upwards, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: short for fabulous
to fling is to throw

explanation.surface: Admiring a mighty upward throw that leaves the spectators puzzled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skyward throw' looks like one action, a toss upwards, but 'skyward' belongs to the word before it, not to the throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Baffling and perplexing are synonyms, both describing something confusing that is hard to understand.

clue.text: Fuddy-duddy Spurs wingers admitting defeat? On the contrary

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so only the outside letters of the word are used
to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside another
this swaps the stated roles, so the piece described as going inside becomes the outer one instead

blocks.note: to foil is to defeat or thwart
the first and last letters of Spurs

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned football fan grumbling that Tottenham's wide players are conceding defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club. As written, the wingers hold the defeat; 'On the contrary' flips that, so the defeat word holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is an informal term for an old-fashioned person stuck in the past, just like a stuffy old fogey.

clue.text: Red army invading quiet zone

indicators.note: an invading force moves into territory, so these letters go inside the others

blocks.note: the call for quiet
the Irish Republican Army
Z is an abbreviation for zone

explanation.surface: A communist army marching into a peaceful area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red army' suggests the Soviet military, but 'Red' is the definition on its own, a red wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiraz is a grape variety and the full-bodied red wine made from it, so it is an example of a red.

clue.text: Fans around India excited after king returned the country's old money

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first letters wrap the next one
excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed into a new order
something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards
after tells you this part comes later, placing the earlier wordplay behind the next piece

blocks.note: Latin for king
taken as written
I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Indian supporters excited when their king came home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The country' points back to India in the clue, so India does double duty: a letter in the wordplay and the place whose coin is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The xerafin was a silver coin formerly used in Portuguese India, so it is historical currency of that land.

clue.text: Right ascending note's creating sound effect

indicators.note: in a down entry, ascending means going upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
a breve is a long musical note

explanation.surface: A musical note climbing up the scale and making an effect in the studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ascending note' sounds like a rising pitch, but the climbing is the note's spelling going upwards in the grid. A breve is a note twice the length of a semibreve.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverb, short for reverberation, is an echo-like audio treatment added in recording and performance.

clue.text: We hear people waiting by new supermarket for a place to buy and sell securities

definitions.text: a place to buy and sell securities

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the spelling is replaced by a letter with the same sound

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
Asda is a British supermarket chain
people waiting in line form a queue, said like the letter Q

explanation.surface: Shoppers lining up outside a newly opened supermarket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' places the waiting people beside the rest, here at the end. Asda is one of Britain's big supermarket chains, owned for years by Walmart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nasdaq is the American stock exchange in New York where shares in many technology firms are traded.

clue.text: Bodyguard following group of engineers - this in case you forgot

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first-named piece is placed second

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a minder is a bodyguard

explanation.surface: A note to someone that a bodyguard is trailing a team of engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash sets the definition off as a self-referential note, as if the clue itself were the reminder. Minder is British slang for a bodyguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder is a prompt or message that helps someone recall something they might overlook.

clue.text: Dell is put inside suitcase

indicators.note: putting something inside means placing it within another piece

blocks.note: a dell is a small valley, a vale
taken as written

explanation.surface: Packing a Dell laptop into a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: Dell looks like the computer brand, but it is a small wooded valley, and 'put inside' sounds like packing luggage rather than placing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A valise is a small travelling bag or case for clothes, used on a trip.

clue.text: Diva halfheartedly drinks one port

indicators.note: with only half a heart, one of the two letters at the centre goes
to drink something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: Maria Callas, the famous opera soprano
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An opera singer, not very keen, sipping a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink being sipped, but it is a harbour town. The heart of the diva's name is a double L; halving it leaves one L.
explanation.definitionFit: Calais is a French ferry port on the Channel, facing Dover.

clue.text: Looking fixedly, wasting little time when producing chemical weapon

indicators.note: to waste something is to lose it, so those letters disappear

blocks.note: staring is looking fixedly
T is the abbreviation for time, little because it is short
as means when

explanation.surface: Someone staring into space and wasting time while making a deadly weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' means the short form, a single letter, not a small amount of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarin is a nerve agent, a toxic compound used in chemical warfare.
